Migration

By: Johann Botha | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How many Malawians are in South Africa? Does anybody know?

Unique Selling Point:
The seemigly uncontrolled influx of foreign nationals into South Africa has lead to the spates of xenophobic attacks in many parts of our country in recent years. Official figures supplied by Stats SA are based on the census and on the recorded figures at our ports of entry. But, while everybody seems to agree that these facts are wrong, no one actually seems to know how many of these people live and work in South Africa

Summary:
In our story on human trafficking from Malawi last year, the Malawian High Commissioner in Pretoria said that she has heard figures of between 5 and 6 million malawians being in South Africa. The organisation Africa check has since published an article where they refute this claim - stating that the real number is less than 100 000. They base this on the official number supplied by STATS SA and also the number supplied by the UN, which in turn, is also based mostly on the Stats SA figures. The Africa Check article quotes 4 different experts saying that the 5-6 million figure given by the Malawian government is too high, yet not one of them supplies counter claims. In fact, they all say that no-one really knows, and that there are problems with the official numbers. The main problems are that the majority of foreign nationals enter the country illegally and the Stats SA figures are based on recorded entries at our border posts. Also, because they are in the country illegaly they are hesitant to admit their true nationalities on a census, or to even take part in such a process. Secondly, the xenophobic attacks of the past years also causes foreigners not to disclose their status. A further problem is that other statistics such as birth rates would also not be a true reflection, as the majority of malawians working in South Africa are male. We interview the same experts as Africa Check, and focus on the problems faced in calculating the figures. We also look at the impact these migrants have on our economy and in a very competitive jobs market. We ask why it is important to understand the magnitude of the influx, to better manage the threat of xenophobia

Script:


Malawi Update - AfricaCheck
In the past decade, the number of Malawians migrating to South Africa has risen sharply. A new industry has evolved around this... so-called called transporters who help desperate people to make it to South Africa. Many of these transporters are nothing but human traffickers, who often enslave the vulnerable women they lure into the unknown.
Ellen I don't know how many men I’ve slept with
Visiting around 20 villages in the Mzimba district, we found only women, children and those too old to work. Some villages were completely empty. Both the catholic priest of the Mzimba diocese and the head of the district hospital confirmed that most men of working age have left and that now the women were following. They said the figure could be as high as a few million, causing huge social instability in the area.
The Malawian High Commissioner in Pretoria told us that most Malawians in South Africa were without documents
Prof trafficking
She was frank about the difficulties of keeping track of the undocumented citizens
High Commissioner I don't have a real figure yet. I've heard of predictions like 6 million or 5 million. But actually we don't have any records of how many Malawians are here.
Richard Ots, heads an international organisation that specialises in migration patterns
Richard
However, last week the organisation Africa Check disputed this number, saying their own research showed that the number is only somewhere between 75 000 and a 100 000, almost 60 times less than the 5 or 6 million.
According to their website, they only investigate “statements of fact”, yet the High Commissioner clearly stated that she doesn't have an accurate figure. The numbers Africa Check use are those released by Stats SA and the UN, which in turn seems mostly gathered from the South African census, the Community Survey done between censuses and from our ports of entry. But, in Africa Check's own analysis Stats SA as well as their other experts all admit that no one knows the real figure. The ports of entry cannot count those who illegally cross borders, and by all accounts we heard, they far outnumber the legal entrants.
Woman jumpa
Africa Check admits that foreign-born nationals may be increasingly cautious of revealing their origins , but our investigation showed this issue may be far greater than they suggest. All the illegal Malawians we interviewed said they would not admit their nationality to officials, for fear of victimisation, deportation or xenophobic attacks.
"So, on the one hand, we have the most senior person representing the Malawian government in South Africa saying that they are working on a figure of 5 – 6 million a figure echoed by other senior officials and reputable people we interviewed.
On the other hand, the South African government and Africa Check's experts believe there are fewer than 100 000, although also admitting that no one knows for a fact. "
Richard
"Overstating the number could lead to increased xenophobia fears, but underestimating this figure and underplaying this very real problem could be an even bigger danger. Reliable data does not currently exist, and this is a problem we should try and resolve before it is too late.
Ultimately, our story was not about investigating the numbers, but to show the unfolding tragedy of real and desperate people..."
